items.title: Anwar ranked 13th among world's 500 most influential Muslims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been ranked 13th in the 2027 edition of The Muslim 500: The World's 500 Most Influential Muslims, published by the Jordan-based Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC). According to the 18th annual edition accessible at https://themuslim500.com, the publication noted that Anwar assumed office as Malaysia's 10th prime minister in November 2022, leading the unity government under the Pakatan Harapan coalition. Anwar reiterated that Malaysia's absolute non-recognition of Israel is permanent," it said.

items.title: Anwar: 'You don't condemn those who "sakau", yet still kiss their hands'
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned why some people continued to defend and honour leaders accused of plundering public funds, even as the government bore the cost of their past financial mismanagement. Anwar, who is also finance minister, cited the government's financial obligations involving Felda, 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Another RM2 billion to RM3 billion goes towards settling 1MDB's debts, while Tabung Haji requires another RM1 billion," he said.

items.title: Anwar: The problem is leaders without principles, not DAP
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said DAP was not the problem in the country's political landscape, but the lack of Malay leaders with principles and integrity. He said leaders should be judged by their character, honesty and ability to serve the people, rather than their race. It is about ensuring that we have Malay leaders with principles.

items.title: Nacsa on amber alert amid unverified cyberattack claims, says Fahmi
items.summary: MELAKA: No particularly worrying cybersecurity incidents have been confirmed so far, based on daily reports from the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said Nacsa's readiness level is currently at amber alert, or moderate, following claims of cyberattacks circulating on social media recently. Fahmi said Nacsa had looked into the claims of cyber intrusions but had yet to verify their authenticity.

items.title: Nvidia shares tumble as CEO resigns, major indices mixed
items.summary: NEW YORK: Nvidia shares sank early Thursday after Chief Executive Jensen Huang resigned from the AI giant following revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. AMD, considered a rival to Nvidia, rose about two percent. Some analysts said Huang's departure won't affect short-term AI projects already in the works.

items.title: Trump calls for Apple ex-CEO Tim Cook to replace Huang at Nvidia
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia, after Huang quit over revelations of two affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy. "Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. Trump, who was close to Huang, said on his Truth Social network.

items.title: Loke maintains decision to resign despite Anwar's call for talks
items.summary: MELAKA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke is standing by his decision to resign as transport minister despite Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for further discussions on the matter. Loke said his resignation was intended to reaffirm DAP's position against former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak being allowed to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. "I have submitted my resignation letter as a cabinet member to express my party's stand on Najib's house arrest.

items.title: Binance heist reveals uphill battle against hackers
items.summary: An elite North Korean hacking group's US$6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold into a massive theft. Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee's computer or credentials are compromised. Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global's OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider.

items.title: Trump's pause on Iran conflict is as costly as new strikes
items.summary: AS United States President Donald Trump weighs his next steps in the Iran war, Gulf energy producers have adapted to a no-war, no-peace reality that is making their operations more expensive and risky. Even without renewed fullscale fighting, those additional costs could help put a floor under global oil prices. Low-intensity conflict is becoming the Middle East's new normal even as the region's crude exports recover.

items.title: Man arrested with suspected syabu in Kudat
items.summary: KUDAT: Police arrested a man after seizing nine packets of suspected syabu weighing 51.06g in Kampung Lodung, Kudat. The man, in his 30s, tested positive for drugs and has six previous criminal records, including three related to offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. Kudat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Haris Ibrahim said the suspect was arrested by a team from the district police headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division at about 2pm.

items.title: NST Leader:Prioritising a healthy ageing reform agenda
items.summary: The longest a human being has lived is 122 years while the average global life expectancy is 74 years. Malaysia's is 74 to 77 years, the oldest ever recorded is 113 years. We must reconfigure retirement and pension systems, lifetime education, employment opportunities, healthcare financing, wealth distribution and inter-generational wealth transfers.

items.title: Police to send team to Pakistan over 130 Malaysians detained in scam raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police will send officers to Pakistan to investigate the detention of 130 Malaysians in a raid on a suspected scam centre in Rawalpindi last month. Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said the officers would meet Pakistani authorities, record statements and examine devices seized during the raid. He said examining the evidence was important to uncover the syndicate's modus operandi, including its alleged use of Royal Malaysia Police uniforms to deceive victims.

items.title: Azalina: Malaysian Bar has right to challenge Najib house arrest decision
items.summary: BANGI: The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Earlier today, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) objected to the Malaysian Bar's bid to challenge the Pardons Board's decision concerning Najib's SRC International Sdn Bhd sentence. On Nov 10, the Bar filed the judicial review application naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents.

items.title: Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entry following investigation
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy at the heart of a scandal at chipmaker Nvidia , left Singapore in February and was barred from re-entering following an investigation into possible offences, Singapore's home affairs ministry said on Thursday. The ministry said Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was investigated for possible offences including buying servers that were exported via Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market. It said the investigation did not concern espionage.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Thursday, Nov 12, 2026
items.summary: Missed what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1576411]] [[nid:1576410]] [[nid:1576409]] [[nid:1576408]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Melaka poised to become national esports training hub
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the proposal had received Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki's backing following its announcement at the Jelajah E-Sports Melaka Biru 2026 programme in Duyong two days ago. "I would like to confirm that the Mara chairman has agreed to turn Mara's TVET institutions in Melaka into a national esports training centre," he said when officiating the Jelajah E-Sports Melaka Biru 2028 programme in Bandar Merlimau here. Zahid, who is also BN chairman, said he wanted Melaka to host a world-level esports championship in 2028.

items.title: Ex-UKMShape director charged with money laundering
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A former director of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) UKMShape has been charged with 21 counts of money laundering involving more than RM1.55 million. Datuk Muhammad Husin, 64, pleaded not guilty to all the charges before Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud today. The money was allegedly derived from an offence involving the use of his position as UKMShape director for personal benefit, including the purchase of personal assets.

items.title: Anwar: No one defied King's decree over Najib's house arrest
items.summary: AYER MOLEK: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied claims that he and the government defied the Yang di-Pertuan Agong over the house arrest of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. He said his relationship with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia remained cordial, adding that the decision on Najib's house arrest was not within his authority. "Certain leaders are claiming that we have defied the King.

items.title: Husband and wife found dead in embrace in Papar sewage pond
items.summary: PAPAR: A husband and wife were found dead in a sewage pond at a pig farm in Kampung Kawari, Papar. Police believe the 52-year-old man slipped into the pond and his 50-year-old wife fell in while trying to save him. Papar district police chief Superintendent Heryan Mohd Tahir said police received information from a member of the public about the discovery at 11.56am.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to step down in big blow to AI boom
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 per cent, will exit the board as well.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar confirms he has yet to receive Loke's resignation letter
items.summary: MELAKA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants to hold further discussions with DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke over his resignation as transport minister. Anwar said he had yet to receive Loke's resignation letter, despite the Seremban member of Parliament announcing his decision two days ago. "I have not received Anthony Loke's resignation letter.

items.title: Foreigner who severed cop's hand had expired passport - Immigration DG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 32-year-old foreigner who severed a policeman's hand in a parang attack in Kepong yesterday was in Malaysia illegally, with his passport having expired in 2020. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the man had previously held a student pass from 2015 to 2018. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad today confirmed that the eight-hour surgery to reattach Thierry's hand at Kuala Lumpur Hospital was successful.

items.title: Unusual shellfish haul draws crowds to Pantai Sabak, Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Large numbers of shellfish believed to be pen shells have washed ashore at Pantai Sabak, drawing crowds of residents eager to collect them. The shellfish were first spotted yesterday evening, with incoming waves bringing more towards the shore. Nor Ain said large numbers continued to wash ashore with each incoming wave, prompting people to collect them in sacks and baskets.

items.title: Cops bust 112 scam syndicates, detain 932 in nationwide operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have busted 112 scam syndicates operating through call centres and detained 932 people in a nationwide operation conducted from Oct 19 to 31. Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said 153 raids were carried out during Op Magpie 01/2026, exceeding the initial target of 100. He said police also conducted 650 proactive inspections of premises during the operation.

items.title: P.I.E net profits almost tripled in Q3
items.summary: Industrial Bhd recorded RM11.52 million net profits for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), almost tripled a year ago when it reported RM4.49 million, on improved factory utilisation and tighter cost controls. Revenue rose four per cent to RM212.48 million from RM204.90 million previously, mainly driven by stronger demand for raw wire and cable as well as wire harness products, which offset weaker revenue from its EMS segment. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, however, PIE Industrial's net profit fell to RM9.12 million from RM25.87 million in the corresponding period last year, while revenue declined 24 per cent to RM535.11 million from RM707.69 million.

items.title: 149 Chinese citizens deported through Penang airport
items.summary: In a statement, the Kedah Immigration Department said all the detainees were men who had previously been held at the Belantik Immigration Depot in Sik. "All the detainees had completed their sentences and undergone deportation proceedings in accordance with the Immigration Act 1959/63 (Act 155) and the Immigration Regulations 1963," it said. The department said all those deported had also been blacklisted in the Immigration Department's system to prevent them from re-entering the country.

items.title: Five things to know about Nvidia
items.summary: NEW YORK: After launching as a small gaming start-up and morphing into the top chip designer for artificial intelligence, US tech giant Nvidia faces unprecedented turbulence after its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a second extramarital affair with an employee. Huang had already acknowledged being "unfaithful" to his wife, reportedly with a woman US intelligence officials believe was a spy for China. Google, for its cloud computing business, is also a major consumer of Nvidia processors, as are Microsoft and Amazon Web Services.

items.title: IOIPG Malaysia Reit's IPO saw 0.59 times oversubscription, offer price fixed lower
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The initial public offering (IPO) of IOI Properties Group Bhd's real estate investment trust (Reit), IOIPG Malaysia Reit, had been oversubscribed by 0.59 times for its public portion. According to IOIPG Malaysia Reit, the Bumiputera's public portion was subscribed at 0.33 times. The non-Bumiputera portion was oversubscribed 1.85 times, with 9,114 applications for 156.76 million units, while the Bumiputera portion received 1,745 applications for 18.24 million units, representing a subscription rate of 0.33 times.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - Nov 12, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Najib seeks second home Najib Razak has asked to use a second residence while serving his sentence under house arrest, but the request cannot be approved under the current terms. HKL surgeons reattach cop's hand HKL surgeons have successfully reattached a policeman's severed hand in an eight-hour operation following an attack in Kepong. Melaka PH vows to scrap seats Pakatan Harapan has pledged to abolish Melaka's seven appointed assembly seats if it wins the state election.

items.title: PKFZ ready to open records, facilitate audits amid cooking oil traceability concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) says it is prepared to provide relevant reports and facilitate regulatory audits amid concerns over the origin, authenticity and traceability of cooking oil products allegedly blended before being re-exported under Malaysian labels. These include the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), SIRIM, the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB). His remarks came after The Edge reported on Nov 4, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil.

items.title: Muhyiddin hopes 'encouraging' reception in Melaka translates into votes
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu has described the encouraging response from voters in the seven state constituencies it is contesting in the Melaka election as a positive sign ahead of polling day on Saturday. Its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party's campaign efforts had made good progress, judging by the encouraging turnout at its programmes in several constituencies since the campaign began. Also present were Bersatu secretary-general and Melaka election director Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali and Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: Malaysian Bar entitled to challenge Pardons Board decision, says Azalina
items.summary: BANGI, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision. The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) today objected to the Malaysian Bar’s bid to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.

items.title: KTMB: MyKomuter50 pass activation begins Nov 16, offering 30 days of unlimited travel on selected routes from Dec 1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The public can start activating the MyKomuter50 Pass on November 16 to enjoy unlimited travel for 30 days on selected KTM Komuter services for RM50, with savings of up to 88 per cent, effective December 1. Alternatively, users can obtain immediate verification at ticket kiosks or counters at KTM Komuter stations. KTMB said activation and purchase facilities would be available at 34 selected stations, comprising 10 KTM Komuter Northern Sector stations, 20 Klang Valley KTM Komuter stations and four Southern Shuttle stations.

items.title: Anwar joins Pakatan campaign trail in Melaka ahead of Saturday’s state polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined the coalition’s campaign trail in Melaka today as campaigning intensified ahead of Saturday’s state election. Anwar’s evening itinerary included the Melaka Rumah Kita programme at the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary service centre in Bukit Baru, followed by Melaka Rumah Kita carnival at Taman Melaka Perdana in Alor Gajah. In the 16th Melaka polls, PH is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 of the 28 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five) and Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (one).

items.title: Malaysia’s FRIM puts century-old library collection online, opening 77,600 digital files to public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — More than a century’s worth of knowledge and information on tropical forest biodiversity and science from the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) is now accessible worldwide through its digital repository, the FRIM Research Depository (FRED). FRIM said in a statement today that the FRED portal, fully operational since last year, recorded an average of 2,885 user accesses annually and offered free registration for round-the-clock access to 160,244 metadata records and 77,600 digital files. Besides preserving heritage manuscripts from physical deterioration, the library houses four major special collections, namely the Rattan Collection, Bamboo Collection, Asean Collection and FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection.

items.title: Malaysia selects Turkiye as preferred alternative missile supplier for Navy’s LCS project, says defence minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Turkiye has been selected as the preferred country to supply an alternative to Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the decision was made after the government evaluated proposals from several countries, including Turkiye, France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs. Mohamed Khaled said the missile from Turkiye was of the same type as that already ordered for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project, allowing supplies to be obtained earlier, as early as 2028.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia must tap China ties to grow exports and open markets for local products
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Malaysia should make the most of its strong ties with China to boost exports and expand markets for local products, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Madani Government would continue to strengthen the business environment and help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) expand their reach in international markets. Anwar said the government fully supported this year's conference as a strategic platform to strengthen trade, investment and business networks between the corporate communities of both countries.

items.title: Twelve Filipinos, including six children, detained in Labuan immigration crackdown
items.summary: LABUAN, Nov 12 — Twelve Filipino nationals, including six children, were detained for suspected immigration offences during an enforcement operation on this duty-free island early today. Labuan Immigration Department director Mohd Redzuan Nawi said the operation, codenamed Op Sapu, was conducted from 11pm yesterday to 1.30am today, involving 15 officers who inspected 84 individuals at several locations, including a residential settlement. Mohd Redzuan said the department would continue enforcing the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passports Act 1966, Immigration Regulations 1963 and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Atipsom).

items.title: Consumers in Malaysia may soon be able to check chicken’s halal status under proposed new rules
items.summary: Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the move was among efforts to strengthen protection for Muslim consumers following concerns raised by members of parliament over the monitoring and transparency of the halal status of chicken supplies. He said KPDN also agreed with a proposal by Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) that responsibility for ensuring the integrity of the halal supply chain should not rest solely with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and state religious authorities, but should also involve KPDN in enforcement and local authorities (PBT) in monitoring business premises. “Therefore, KPDN will propose better coordination with state religious authorities, local authorities and the Health Ministry to improve the monitoring of slaughterhouses and chicken sales premises,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Four foreigners arrested over robbery, assault of cop in Penang; remanded for six days until Nov 17
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — Penang police have arrested four Pakistani nationals, including two women, to assist in investigations into a robbery in which a 43-year-old policeman was injured by suspects armed with sharp objects near a petrol station in Permatang Pauh on Tuesday. Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the four suspects, aged between 23 and 36, had been remanded for six days until November 17 to facilitate investigations. The policeman was injured after being robbed by four suspects armed with sharp objects near the entrance to a petrol station in Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, on Tuesday.

items.title: Man hanging cat from four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang sparks online outrage
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 12 — A video and an image showing a man hanging a cat by its neck from the window of a four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang, Johor, have sparked outrage on social media. Several social media posts claimed the incident took place at Batu Dua, Jalan Mersing, in Kluang. Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police had not received any reports regarding the alleged incident.

items.title: Malaysia approves 143 posts for new Public Defender’s Office, says Azalina
items.summary: “This marks a new chapter for the Legal Aid Department (JBG). As we discussed during the debate on amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, we looked at the roles the government should play alongside the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), as a substantial amount of government funding goes directly to YBGK. She said the initiative would complement the existing legal aid services provided by JBG under the Legal Aid Act by offering another avenue for alternative dispute resolution.

items.title: Malaysia’s fiscal reforms set to lower federal debt ratio to 63.7pc by 2027, says Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Madani government is committed to gradually reducing the fiscal deficit from 5.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022 to 3.3 per cent in 2027. Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the reduction in the fiscal deficit reflects the government’s commitment to strengthen the country’s financial position, thereby helping to lower the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP. He said the government still prioritises efforts to increase people’s income, including through a minimum wage increase.

items.title: Anwar chairs special meeting as Selangor steps up efforts to tackle recurring floods
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today chaired a special meeting on Selangor flood disaster coordination at Parliament House to streamline efforts to address recurring floods in the state. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting focused on four key actions, including strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving disaster management coordination by the Selangor State Disaster Management Committee. Amirudin said the meeting was also attended by state government representatives, state executive councillors, state assemblymen, district officers, and relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), DID, the Public Works Department (JKR), and the Selangor Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU).

items.title: Kelantan reassigns Culture and Heritage portfolio to Zamakshari Muhamad after Kamaruddin Mohd Noor dropped from exco
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 12 — Kelantan Youth, Sports, NGOs and Community Unity Committee chairman Zamakshari Muhamad has been entrusted with overseeing the state’s Culture and Heritage portfolio. He said Kelantan had a distinct cultural identity, rich in historical values, traditions, arts and local wisdom, which formed part of the identity of its people. “I will focus on efforts to preserve and document historical heritage and customs, as well as strengthen local arts and culture in line with Islamic principles and the values of Kelantan society.

items.title: Sarawak targets year-end pilot launch for ART service on Rembus-Northbank route, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 12 — Pilot operations of the Autonomous Rapid Transit (ART) service along the initial Rembus-Northbank route are targeted to begin by the end of this year, said Caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg. He said the service would further integrate Samarahan into the Kuching Urban Transportation System (KUTS), which uses ART technology as a key component of Sarawak’s modern public transport network. Abang Johari said commercial ART services would be introduced in stages following the pilot phase.

items.title: Sarawak deputy premier says NCR land surveys will only proceed with owners’ consent
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 12 — Native Customary Rights (NCR) land ownership in Sarawak continues to be protected through land surveys conducted only upon the application and consent of stakeholders to prevent boundary disputes, encroachment and the loss of rights to ancestral land. Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan said every survey application must undergo scrutiny and verification of ownership evidence by the Sarawak Land and Survey Department to ensure the claims are legally valid. “We want to avoid misunderstandings or allegations that the government is attempting to seize people’s land,” he said at the presentation ceremony for Native Communal Reserve gazette notifications, land titles and land compensation cheques for Sibu Division here today.

items.title: Penang to consult stakeholders on raising Muslim marriage age to 18
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — The Penang government will hold engagement sessions to explore the possibility of raising the minimum age for Muslims to marry to 18, following similar moves by Selangor and Kedah. Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Mohamad Abdul Hamid, who is also Penang Islamic Religious Council (MAINPP) president, said the sessions would be held to gather views and assess whether the proposed change could be implemented in the state. Mohamad said the minimum age for Muslims to marry in Penang remained 16.

items.title: Sabah Fire Dept urges public to avoid rivers, waterfalls during monsoon
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 12 — The public is reminded to adhere to safety advice and take necessary precautions when dealing with floods, as well as to postpone all water-based recreational activities during the current North-east Monsoon (MTL) season. Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Mohd Pisar Aziz said residents must immediately move to relief centres when instructed by the authorities or if rising floodwaters threaten their homes. Mohd Pisar also advised the public to postpone all water-based recreational activities, including bathing, swimming, picnicking and camping near rivers, rapids, waterfalls and irrigation canals throughout the Northeast Monsoon season.

items.title: Malaysia tightens screening of foreign students to protect higher education standards
items.summary: Commenting on language requirements, Azlinda said all foreign students, including postgraduate students, were required to undergo a one-semester Bahasa Melayu course upon enrolment at local universities, particularly public universities (UA). Meanwhile, she said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) and the NAMA Foundation were actively mobilising efforts to secure funding contributors to offer full and partial scholarship schemes for international students. Azlinda said the funding initiative could help cover students’ living expenses while driving the target of attracting 500,000 international students by 2035 under the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint (RPTM) 2026-2035, compared with approximately 170,000 currently.

items.title: Deep-rooted discrimination leaves Malaysian Indian youths feeling alienated and marginalised, report finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Indian youths in Malaysia are feeling increasingly marginalised, facing systemic discrimination in education, employment, and housing that leaves many feeling politically alienated, according to a new report by think tank Iman Research. The report, titled Kami Orang Sini Juga — Indian Youth Report , launched today, highlights that this demographic is an “under-mobilised constituency” whose concerns have long been overlooked by policymakers and the political establishment. “Indian youths are an under-mobilised constituency whose concerns have been ignored for too long.

items.title: Malaysian Indian youths see education system as source of discrimination, Iman Research report finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Indian youths in Malaysia see the national education system as a significant source of discrimination rather than a pathway to social mobility, according to a report released today by Iman Research. The study, titled The Kita Orang Sini Juga – Indian Youth Report , found that students experienced social alienation and institutional bias throughout their schooling, sometimes at the hands of those responsible for guiding their development. The report cited a 2021 survey by youth movement Sekolah Semua, which found that nine in 10 Indian students felt they had experienced discrimination because of their ethnicity; based on 2,441 responses nationwide, 73 per cent said they faced discrimination from their peers, while 74 per cent reported similar experiences involving teachers.

items.title: Penang CM: Loke’s resignation ‘painful’, but shows his principles
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook’s resignation as transport minister was a “painful” decision but reflected his willingness to take responsibility based on principles, said Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow. Chow said Loke’s decision was not an easy one, especially given the public attention surrounding a court decision involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. “I view Anthony Loke’s resignation as a decision that pains us.

items.title: Flood evacuee numbers in Selangor, Perak fall from 1,484 to 1,445 as of 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The number of flood evacuees sheltering at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak fell slightly this afternoon to 1,445 people from 405 families, down from 1,484 people from 420 families this morning. In Selangor, the number of victims housed at relief centres in Kuala Selangor dropped to 1,144 as of 4pm, compared with 1,180 this morning. According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed 391 evacuees, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (283), SK Parit Mahang (248), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (71), and SK Jaya Setia (12).

items.title: Altantuya case: Mongolia urges Malaysia to seek Sirul’s return with guarantee against execution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Mongolia has formally asked Malaysia to intensify talks with Australia for the lawful return of convicted former police officer Sirul Azhar Umar, with effective assurances against the death penalty, as part of a diplomatic push over Altantuya Shaariibuu’s murder. In a statement today, Mongolia’s special envoy Zandanshatar Gombojav said his government also wanted lawful ways identified for Sirul, currently in Australia, to testify in the civil proceedings. The requests follow Mongolia’s expression of profound regret over the Court of Appeal’s January 20, 2026 ruling reversing the Malaysian government’s civil liability for the killing, although it reaffirmed respect for Malaysia’s judicial independence.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Youths aged 18 to 39 account for nearly one million voters in the state
items.summary: Sin Chew Daily reported that voters aged 30 to 39 totalled 441,884, while 405,499 voters were aged between 21 and 29. In the senior categories, a total of 239,281 voters are aged from 60 to 69, followed by the 70 to 79 age group with 132,303 voters, 80 to 89 age group (40,173 voters), and aged 90 and above group (13,146 voters). In Padungan, the number of voters aged from 60 to 69 stood at 5,636, followed by the 70 to 79 age group (4,738 voters), 80 to 89 age group (1,873 voters), and 90 and above group (473 voters).

items.title: Seven scam syndicates targeting victims overseas busted in Sarawak, 28 foreigners among 42 held
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 12 — Police have dismantled seven online scam syndicates operating in Sarawak and arrested 42 individuals, including 28 foreign nationals, during a series of raids under Op Magpie 01/2026. Sarawak police commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said the operation, coordinated by the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department’s Operations Intelligence Division, was carried out simultaneously across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak to combat organised scam call centre activities. Between October 19 and 31, seven separate raids were conducted in Bintulu, Kuching, Padawan, Miri, and Sibu, targeting syndicates operating out of residential properties — specifically two bungalows, three terraced houses, and two apartment units.

items.title: Saifuddin to suggest declassifying Pardons Board meeting minutes to Cabinet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told Parliament today that he would try to put forward proposals to declassify the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes involving Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Razak at tomorrow's Cabinet meeting. Saifuddin earlier took on questions about the conditions around Najib's house arrest, which began on Tuesday after the former prime minister secured a fresh High Court order allowing his transfer from Kajang Prison to his residence on Jalan Langgak Duta here. Najib's lawyers had indicated they would appeal.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan pledges to abolish seven appointed assemblymen seats if elected
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has pledged to repeal the state legislation allowing the appointment of seven Melaka state assembly members if it wins the mandate to govern the state in the 16th Melaka election. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said savings from abolishing the appointed seats would be channelled towards homeownership assistance for young people and programmes to develop young entrepreneurs. “The provision allowing seven appointed assembly members was approved by the State Legislative Assembly under the previous Barisan Nasional administration.

items.title: Four men convicted in Wang Kelian mass graves case repatriated to Thailand
items.summary: KANGAR, Nov 12 — Six Thai nationals, including four convicted in a case linked to migrant smuggling camps and the discovery of mass graves in Wang Kelian in 2015, were repatriated to Thailand yesterday after completing their prison sentences in Malaysia. Perlis Immigration director Mohammad A’sim Md Ali said the four men, aged between 31 and 61, were extradited from Thailand to Malaysia in June 2023 to face legal proceedings. Mohammad A’sim said the court ordered their sentences to run from June 22, 2023, the date of their arrest.
